summary:
This L0009 run started at 08:04 UTC on Nov 26 from the line's timer, not from an instruction. It had no 'Asked' items, so the empty answers list is right. It made no claims and changed none. It did three things. It collected the seed 1, f* 0.3 crawl layer left by the previous run. It fixed the same-instant loop in two code changes on branch method/rest, decisions D0091 and D0092, tested as E0106 (falsified) and E0107 (supported). It committed an untested plate check, D0093. The main findings stand and reproduce. Two ledger outcome records carry wrong numbers that were not corrected. Pre-registration was again not quite before the runs. The pinned algorithm page says more than the code does.

What reproduces. I ran E0107's code (607b687) myself with the session's script, scripts/rest_plate/feed_run.py, for seed 1 and seed 2 at f* 0.3. Apart from CPU times, both result files match the session's in every field. The step logs are identical line for line. Seed 1 stops with 'sphere penetrates the bottom plate' after reaching 5.88, with 33 stacks built, 5 joins and the pull rule used once. Seed 2 stops the same way after 6.22, with 19,779 fallback collisions. All eighteen data files in runs/E0105, E0106 and E0107 match their recorded SHA-256 and sizes. The logs say what the session says. E0106 matches E0105 step for step in all three layers up to where E0105 stopped. E0107 matches E0106 up to 5.87 in seed 1 and is identical in seed 2. So D0091 acted only at the loop instant: its 30 uses in E0106 are the 30 repeats of the new loop, which the evidence file says. In the f* 0.4 layer, E0107 differs from E0106 by a handful of counts (89 against 88 stacks broken, 168 against 166 touch contacts), so D0092 acted there too.

I read D0092's code in edmd.py first_contact_any. The probe step is the right root of the gap's lower bound under the existing second-derivative bound M. A pair is skipped only if it turns around before its squared gap goes below -1e-13. That limits skipped approaches to normal speeds of roughly a millionth (from the square root of 2 M times 2e-13), a hundred times or more below the rest speed of 0.01. So 'no constant added' holds in substance: the floor already existed, and it now also decides what counts as a touch. Dropping a pulling contact (D0091) changes no velocity, so it cannot inject energy. No layer finished a cycle, so no energy audit exists to check. The engine's gain counter is zero in every layer. The largest gain at a touch is 7e-16, in f* 0.4 only.

Seed 2 trace (my own, scratch, about 100 s CPU). The line state says seed 2 'stops the same way at 6.22', while the summary only says 'probably the same cause (not traced)'. I traced it. Sphere 54 was in a three-sphere stack with spheres 60 and 67, with no plate contact. At the break at t = 6.22478, caused by sphere 67 touching sphere 60, it was handed back free, 1.8e-7 below the plate. The plate search then raised the error. So the state sentence holds: it is the same fault as seed 1, with a sink of 1.8e-7 rather than 4.65e-5. The trace also shows where seed 2's 19,779 fallback collisions come from. Just before the break, the stack event between spheres 54 and 60 repeats at times 6.22443247464945 to 6.22443247464951, advancing by about 1e-14 each time. That is a near-same-instant loop, which the loop detector misses because it counts only calls at exactly one time. The 'next' item lists those collisions as their own problem. They are this loop.

What is wrong.
(1) The ledger outcomes carry wrong numbers that were never corrected. E0106's outcome says 'touch_max_gain 0' for every layer, but f* 0.4 had 7.1e-16. The summary admits this but appends no correcting record. E0107's outcome says the f* 0.4 run 'was still crawling at 5.25 at the end of this run'. Its result file, collected at 08:43, says it reached 5.27 and was stopped by the CPU cap at 5.276 after 1200 s. Both outcomes are also wrong about seed 1. 'Completes the step to 5.88 (33 stacks built, 5 joins, 33 broken)': the step log shows 30 built and 28 broken at the end of the step to 5.88. The 33 is the count at the stop inside the step to 5.89. The summary repeats 'finished the step to 5.88, building 33 stacks'. Neither error changes a status: E0106 is still falsified and E0107 still supported. But the ledger is what the map shows, and it should get correcting records.
(2) The pinned algorithm page (lines/L0009/pinned/current-algorithm.md) says the pull rule applies at the 'start of any stack (built, joined, or split)'. In the code (sim.py _stack_new), it catches only a pull found by the check made before the first span. A pull found once integration of the first span has begun still goes through the old path: the start is refused and every sphere handed back unchanged. In E0107 that happened 45 times in the f* 0.4 layer, twice in seed 2 and once in seed 1, all with the reason 'contact pulls'. The f* 0.4 refusals repeat the same pull force (N = -0.896903) 26 times. That fits the crawl being this refusal recurring a little later each time, but I have not shown that. The summary's first proposed direction ('apply the pull rule at span restarts too') points at this, but the page does not. The same page says the best layer is 'seed 1, f* 0.3 reaches 5.88 of 7.45'. Seed 2 at f* 0.3 got further, to 6.22.
(3) Pre-registration again came after the runs started, though only by ten seconds. The E0106 runs started at 08:07:01. The registration commit is at 08:07:11, and its 'at' time of 08:07:30 is later than both. The summary says so itself. E0107 was registered properly: commit at 08:14:49, runs started at 08:14:53. The decisions' 'at' times are still estimates, not measured. The summary's 'ended' time now matches the final commit, which answers last review's point.
(4) Budget: the summary gives 829.1 CPU-hours spent. program check gives 820.6 (8%), and that figure already includes this run's outcomes. The summary is about 8.5 hours high. Both are far below 50%.

Smaller points. The line note says as fact that 'local jobs here do not outlive the run'. The evidence (the process gone, and a new process-number space each run) makes it likely, not shown. The line state's 'no touch has gained energy' is true to round-off (7e-16). For the bounce question to Chris: E0107's seed 1 run has no loop repeats and gives a larger sample. There, 31 of 38 touches on stack spheres were at or above the rest speed and one was at or above the wake speed, so the bounce rule would have kept 30 of those stacks. Since there is no instruction, all the work served the line's own 'next', which is appropriate for a timer run.

Last review's points. All answered. The seed 1 touch numbers without the loop repeats (23, 18, 1, median 0.017, median lifetime 0.00047) are now in evidence/E0105-collection.json, and seed 2 is in the question. The f* 0.4 job ended without a result, as I predicted (no result file, log stopped at 5.25). The CPU cap is now checked at every stack handler call, and it worked: both f* 0.4 runs stopped at 1200 s. A0199 was re-recorded with its five files. active.jsonl is empty. The timestamps of 'ended' and the line records now match the commits.

Line state for L0009. Every sentence holds after my checks, including 'seed 2 stops the same way', which my trace confirms. The 'next' should say that seed 2's 19,779 fallback collisions are a near-same-instant loop on spheres 54 and 60.

Housekeeping. program check passes, except for my own scratch folder checker/, which I removed before committing. The latest approval is approved/20261124T031934, more than a day old. The data folder is 716 megabytes of the 15 gigabyte limit, with 82 gigabytes free against a floor of 40. tmp/ is empty. Nothing was written outside the program folders in the run's window except the uv cache in ~/.cache/uv, which the program tool itself uses.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 08:04:19, nineteen seconds after its scheduled time. Its last commit was at 08:44:26, inside the hour. It got a lot done: the old job was collected, two fixes were tested, the next fault was traced, and a third fix was committed. The untested plate check (D0093) is left waiting on finding out why a trace with it ran five times slower. The machine did not limit the science: load was low, there was 82 GB of free disk, the data folder is 716 MB, and the CPU caps of 1200 s per layer were the session's own choice. The recorded 1.11 CPU-hours matches the sum of its parts (1556 + 229 + 1200 + 579 + 390 + 40 s). pmset and ps are absent on this Linux worker, so I could not check for sleep. The 10-minute 'interruption' was a wait on the session's own trace.
discrepancies: The E0106 registration is stamped 08:07:30, but its commit is at 08:07:11 and its runs started at 08:07:01 (disclosed in the summary).
The summary's budget says 829.1 CPU-hours spent; program check says 820.6, including this run.
E0107's outcome says the f* 0.4 run was still crawling at 5.25; its collected result says it was stopped by its CPU cap at 5.276 after 1200 s.
